skill.name: chapter-outline-generator
skill.description: Generates detailed chapter outlines for books, including key scenes, plot progression, character arcs, and themes. Use this when planning book structure or expanding story ideas.
skill.summary: Creates structured chapter outlines with plot beats, character moments, themes, and transitions.
skill.author: Amraha-Anwar

security_audit.summary: No static findings were reported, and review of SKILL.md found prompt-only writing guidance. No prompt injection, code execution, network access, filesystem access, or credential-handling behavior was found.

content.user_title: Plan Book Chapters With Structured Outlines
content.value_statement: Turning a story idea into chapters can be slow and inconsistent. This skill creates a structured chapter plan with key scenes, arcs, themes, and transitions.
actual_capabilities: Collects missing basics such as title, genre, plot summary, and chapter count.
Organizes chapter plans around common narrative beats and story arcs.
Defines chapter titles, key events, conflicts, character moments, tone, and themes.
Adds subplots, foreshadowing, lore notes, and transitions between chapters.
Produces a Markdown list with clear sub-points for each chapter.
Checks that the sequence supports continuity and avoids obvious contradictions.
limitations: It creates outlines, not full manuscript chapters.
Output quality depends on the premise, genre, and chapter count supplied by the user.
It may need author review for voice, pacing, and genre-specific expectations.
It does not replace professional editing, sensitivity review, or factual research.

use_cases.title: Novel Structure Planning
use_cases.description: Turn a premise into a chapter-by-chapter plan before drafting the manuscript.

use_cases.title: Story Development Review
use_cases.description: Map plot progression, character growth, and escalation points for early story feedback.

use_cases.title: Classroom Writing Projects
use_cases.description: Help students organize long-form stories into coherent chapters with clear narrative beats.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Outline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a clear premise.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a chapter outline for a [genre] book titled [title]. The main plot is [summary]. Use [number] chapters.

prompt_templates.title: Expand a Story Idea
prompt_templates.scenario: Develop a short concept into a full structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a detailed chapter outline from this story idea: [idea]. Include setup, inciting incident, rising action, midpoint, climax, and resolution.

prompt_templates.title: Strengthen Character Arcs
prompt_templates.scenario: Focus the outline on character development.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [number]-chapter outline for [title]. Track how [main character] changes across the story and include key emotional turning points.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Complex Narrative
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with multiple plot threads.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a chapter outline for [title] with [number] chapters. Include the main plot, two subplots, foreshadowing, lore details, themes, and chapter transitions.

output_examples.input: A twelve-chapter fantasy novel about a mapmaker who discovers a living map.
output: Chapter 1: The Map That Breathes. Introduces the mapmaker, the city, and the strange artifact.
Chapter 6: The Border Moves. The midpoint reveals that the map changes the real world.
Chapter 12: The Last Landmark. The final choice resolves the conflict and completes the character arc.

output_examples.input: A mystery outline that emphasizes clues, suspects, and chapter endings.
output: Each chapter includes a clue, a false lead, a suspect interaction, and a tension-building transition.
The outline places the midpoint discovery before the second major reversal.
The ending connects the motive, evidence, and character consequences.

best_practices: Provide the genre, intended chapter count, main conflict, and ending preference.
Name important characters and explain how they should change by the final chapter.
Review the outline for pacing before asking for scene-level expansion.
anti_patterns: Do not request a detailed outline without giving a premise or story goal.
Do not treat the first outline as final without checking continuity and pacing.
Do not use the outline as a substitute for drafting scenes in the author voice.

faq.question: Can this skill outline nonfiction books?
faq.answer: It is designed for narrative books, but it can support memoir or story-driven nonfiction with clear chapter goals.

faq.question: Does it write full chapters?
faq.answer: No. It creates chapter outlines with events, themes, character moments, and transitions.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the book title, genre, main plot summary, number of chapters, and major character goals.

faq.question: Can it handle subplots?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions ask for subplots, foreshadowing, lore, and transitions when creating chapter details.

faq.question: Will it check continuity?
faq.answer: Yes. It is instructed to keep the sequence logical and avoid contradictions.
